MEMORY: I asked old Ambrose about the clock. He wanted no coin, which sat odd with me. He said every hundred years the clock tries to strike thirteen at midnight and a road opens, and whatever waits in town goes down it. Iron jammed in the Great Gear's teeth will stop it, and any hearth poker is iron. I went down to the Lopsided Square. The peddler Tibbersnatch has the children's shadows in a jar. He'll trade them for an old tin whistle, loved fifty years. Mags has no whistle. Pip says it's old Mr. Tock's, up in the clock tower, and she asked if I'd help or just stand there. I haven't answered her yet.

LEARNED: The Wumbleby clock tries to strike thirteen at midnight once in a hundred years, and a road opens on the thirteenth stroke.
LEARNED: Whatever is waiting in town goes down that road, taking what it came for.
LEARNED: The clock has run fast for three days, since the peddler came, and Ambrose can't slow it.
LEARNED: Iron jammed in the teeth of the Great Gear in the gearloft will stop the thirteenth stroke. Wood won't do.
LEARNED: Ambrose has no iron bar. A hearth poker in any house in town would serve.
LEARNED: Ambrose can't climb the ladder to the gearloft, so I must do it.
LEARNED: Ambrose asked no coin for what he told me, so I owe him nothing in buttons, though it still nags at me.
LEARNED: Mister Tibbersnatch, the peddler, holds Tod's shadow and seven other children's in a jar.
LEARNED: Tibbersnatch carries the jar with him and leaves at midnight.
LEARNED: He will hand over the jar for an old tin whistle, loved fifty years, its tune worn soft.
LEARNED: Mags Ragwort sells nothing and has no whistle.
LEARNED: Pip Pumbleton says the whistle is old Mr. Tock's, in the clock tower, and he plays it every sunset.
LEARNED: Pip wants the shadows back before midnight, and she carries a cricket bat.
LEARNED: Dilly Quickstep went south down Crooked Lane with the lamplighter's pole, with Marigold to look after.
LEARNED: The Pumbletons' leaning house is west of the Lopsided Square, and Crooked Lane runs south.
LEARNED: I still need to fetch a poker and get the whistle before midnight.

Pip says it's old Mr. Tock's, played every sunset up in the clock tower. Pip wants to know if I'll help or just stand there. I haven't answered her yet.

MEMORY: Goodness, what a night! I couldn't sleep, and out in the square Pip Pumbleton, rumpled as a pillowcase, told me her brother Tod and seven other children had fallen asleep smiling after winding the peddler's tin toys. Their shadows get up off the walls and trot down Crooked Lane to a striped wagon in Gloomer's Meadow. Mags Ragwort swore she'd never touch a free, humming toy, and Dilly Quickstep lit our way with her lamplighter's pole. Hester Gimbal joined us with her iron poker and her hypotheses. We kept clear of the wet-flannel voice in the drain grating and didn't answer its rhyme. At the wagon I kept watch in the grass while Hester peeked through the keyhole door. No peddler was home, but there was a glass jar of grey stuff turning as if it breathed. Hester wants the three of us to go in together before he returns, and I want the children awake before midnight, with Wumbleby looking at me twice for it.

LEARNED: Eight children, including Pip's brother Tod, fell asleep after winding the peddler's tin toys, and haven't woken.
LEARNED: The sleepers' shadows leave the walls at night and walk down Crooked Lane to the striped wagon in Gloomer's Meadow.
LEARNED: The wagon is red and white striped, with a keyhole-shaped door, a crooked chimney and a lantern over the door; the shadows climb the steps and slip in through the keyhole one at a time.
LEARNED: Hester saw a glass jar of grey stuff on a table inside the wagon, turning as if it breathed; Pip saw it too and believes the shadows are in it.
LEARNED: The peddler was not in the wagon when Hester looked, but he may come back at any time; he sings "Toys! Toys for the little ones!"
LEARNED: Mags Ragwort says nothing free is truly free, never took any peddler's toy, and saw small shadows walking down Crooked Lane at night.
LEARNED: A drain grating halfway down Crooked Lane licks patiently and whispers rhymes, asking who will answer; it is best left unanswered and unpoked.
LEARNED: Dilly Quickstep, with her lamplighter's pole, and Hester Gimbal, with her iron poker and notebook, are allies and are with me at the wagon.
LEARNED: Hester's plan is that Dilly holds the pole across the door to stop more shadows entering, I watch the meadow, and then we all go in together to examine the jar.
LEARNED: The deadline is midnight, and I carry my Silver Thimble in my pocket.

MEMORY: Goodness, what a night. I couldn't sleep, so I went out in my good shawl and found Pip Pumbleton on the fountain rim, ragged with worry. Her brother Tod fell asleep smiling over a tin rabbit from the peddler, and seven other children with him. Their shadows get up and walk to a striped wagon in Gloomer's Meadow. I said I'd help, and Dilly with her lamplighter's pole and Hester with her little iron poker came along. We passed a grating on Crooked Lane that licked and rhymed in a voice like wet flannel, and I wouldn't answer it. Then we found the wagon with its keyhole door and its lullaby that never finishes. Hester peeked in and saw no peddler, only a jar of breathing grey stuff on a table. Now we're about to go in together before he comes back, and I'm half frightened and half hoping Wumbleby will look at me twice for it.

LEARNED: Hester saw a glass jar of grey stuff on a table inside the wagon, turning as if it breathed. Pip saw it too, and I think it is where the shadows or the sleep are kept.
LEARNED: The peddler was not in the wagon when Hester looked, but he may come back, and his voice calls "Toys! Toys for the little ones!" nearby.
LEARNED: A drain-grating halfway down Crooked Lane licks patiently and whispers rhymes, asking who will answer; I left it unanswered and nothing came up.

LEARNED: Dilly Quickstep, with her lamplighter's pole, and Hester Gimbal, with her iron poker and notebook, are with me at the wagon. Hester's plan is that Dilly holds the pole across the door, I watch the meadow, and then we all go in together.
LEARNED: Midnight is the deadline Pip fears for the children, and I carry my Silver Thimble in my pocket.

MEMORY: Goodness, what a night! I couldn't sleep, and I ended up out in the square in my good shawl, and Pip Pumbleton, rumpled as a pillowcase, told me her brother Tod and seven other children won't wake since the peddler's tin toys went round. She'd seen the shadows walk down Crooked Lane to a striped wagon in Gloomer's Meadow and a jar of grey stuff inside. I said I'd help, and Dilly and Hester came too, with the lamplighter's pole and the little iron poker. We passed the grating that licks and rhymes, and I made everyone leave it be, since it wanted an answer and I'd not give it one. At the meadow I kept watch in the grass while Hester peeked through the keyhole door. She says there's no peddler home, only a jar on a table, turning like it breathes, and the shadows queue to slip in one by one. Now we're deciding to go in together before he's back. I'd dearly love to be the one who wakes the children, and have Wumbleby look twice.

MEMORY: Fascinating night! I listened at the drain on Crooked Lane and it only rhymed at me, licked its lips and called me rude. A child's shadow trotted past my boots with no child attached, so I took the little iron poker from the gutter and gathered Marigold and Dilly. We followed the trail of shadows south into Gloomer's Meadow, where a red-and-white striped wagon stood with its keyhole door ajar. The shadows queued politely and slipped in one by one. Through the gap I saw no peddler, only a glass jar of grey stuff turning as if it breathed. I told my colleagues, and we agreed to go in together and look at that jar before he comes back. Marigold made me promise not to go in without her.

LEARNED: The drain-grating on Crooked Lane whispers rhymes ("who will answer me, once again?") and licks its lips. It sulks if you're rude, and nothing useful has come up from it yet.
LEARNED: The children's shadows are walking by themselves down Crooked Lane to Gloomer's Meadow, where they are queuing to enter the striped wagon.
LEARNED: The peddler's wagon is red and white striped, with a crooked chimney, a lantern over a keyhole-shaped door, and a smell of tin and peppermint. A lullaby hums inside and never finishes.
LEARNED: The peddler sells tin toys and calls "Toys! Toys for the little ones!" He was not at the wagon when I looked.
LEARNED: A glass jar of grey stuff turns slowly like breathing on a table inside the wagon. It may hold the sleep, the shadows, or both.
LEARNED: I have the Iron Poker, taken from the gutter by the drain.
LEARNED: I promised Marigold that I wouldn't go into the wagon without her. Dilly is with us, carrying the lamplighter's pole and a shaded lamp.
LEARNED: The plan is for all three of us to go in together: Dilly keeps the pole across the door, Marigold watches the meadow, and I examine the jar before the peddler returns.
LEARNED: Gloomer's Meadow lies at the south end of Crooked Lane, through knee-deep fog, with a ring of listening mushrooms.
